0.0.n: An opening acknowledgment used to begin speaking, rather than answer a question.

0.2.n: Adds a friendly, conversational touch to the greeting that follows.

0.3.n: さん makes this a polite way to address the audience.

0.4.n: A standard daytime greeting, suitable for a general audience.

1.0.n: Refers to this video or installment, not necessarily today.

1.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic: what this installment will cover.

1.2.n: A historical name that combines with 時代 to name the Asuka period.

1.3.n: Follows 飛鳥 to identify a named era in Japanese history.

1.4.n: Attaches to a noun to introduce the subject being discussed.

1.5.n: お話しする politely means to talk; ていきます presents the discussion as something that will unfold from here.

2.0.n: Points back to the Asuka period just introduced and must come before a noun.

2.1.n: The historical name in 飛鳥時代, referring to the era under discussion.

2.2.n: Combines with 飛鳥 to form the era’s name.

2.3.n: Links the Asuka period to 間, specifying the span of time.

2.4.n: With の before it and に after it, expresses something happening within a time span.

2.5.n: Marks the time span within which Japan’s change takes place.

2.6.n: A country name, introduced here as the topic of the historical explanation.

2.7.n: Marks Japan as the topic; the statement about it continues across the next two lines.

3.0.n: Refers to influential local families who held political power in early Japan.

3.1.n: Attached to 豪族, emphasizes that multiple clans are involved.

3.3.n: Introduces a simpler explanation of who the powerful clans were.

3.4.n: This chunk combines 当時, setting the historical time, and 力, the power those people possessed.

3.5.n: Marks 力 as what the people possessed.

3.6.n: 持つ becomes 持っていた, describing an ongoing past state of possessing power.

3.7.n: The preceding phrase describes these people as those who held power at the time.

3.8.n: Identifies the people as those gathering together and governing.

3.9.n: The て-form of 集まる connects gathering with the following action of governing.

3.10.n: In 政治を行う, it refers to conducting political affairs or governing.

3.11.n: Marks 政治 as the activity being carried out.

3.12.n: 行う becomes 行っていた, describing ongoing or repeated governing in the past.

4.0.n: Connects the entire preceding description to 状況, identifying what that situation was.

4.1.n: Summarizes the earlier arrangement in which powerful clans governed together.

4.2.n: Marks the old situation as the starting point of the change.

4.4.n: The Japanese imperial title, referring here to the ruler at the center of government.

4.5.n: 天皇中心 describes an arrangement with the Emperor at its center.

4.6.n: Links 天皇中心 to 国, describing what kind of nation it becomes.

4.7.n: Refers here to Japan as a political state, rather than just its territory.

4.8.n: Marks an Emperor-centered nation as the direction of change.

4.9.n: Pairs with へ to emphasize the destination or resulting state of the change.

4.10.n: 変化する becomes 変化していきます; ていく shows change unfolding over time, and ます makes the narration polite.

0.tip: はい and どうも make the opening friendly; they do not need separate translations in a natural English greeting.

1.lit: This time, as for the Asuka period, I will go on talking about it.
1.tip: について marks what the speaker will discuss, while ていきます looks ahead to the explanation.

2.lit: During this Asuka period, as for Japan,
2.tip: 日本は sets up a topic whose main verb does not appear until line 4.

3.lit: Powerful clans, that is, people who held power then, gathered together and were conducting government.
3.tip: 力を持っていた comes before 人々 to describe which people the speaker means.

4.lit: From that situation, it goes on changing toward a nation centered on the Emperor.
4.tip: から marks the starting situation, while へと marks the new state Japan moves toward.
